- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.2) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (sentiment drops below 0.1) — adjust downward by 3–8% to avoid overcorrection.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overpredict early in the 30-day horizon — apply a 1–3 day lag correction for the first 5–7 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment > 0.4 and forecast > true outcome by >5%, cap forecast at 10% below true peak.
- Horizon-specific: last 3–5 days of forecast often overestimate — reduce by 2–5% for days 25–30.
- Negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.2) triggers downward bias correction — reduce forecast by 3–7% unless price is already near support.
